property_summary: For any input arguments, calling initialize(...) on a fresh C instance must succeed (not revert) and leave c.initialized() == true; the mutant that sets initialized = true before checking AlreadyInitialized can cause initialize to revert (breaking the rule) for some inputs.
change_summary: Move the initialized = true assignment to the start of initialize() so it becomes true before the AlreadyInitialized check (allowing reverts to still see initialized true in some cases).
